::: {.why}
Your store grew by accretion and the queries you now run are not the ones it was designed for, which is normal and worth one day of correction before phase 11 depends on it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the three schema decisions that matter for a time series store and justify yours.
- Report the query time improvement from the change you make.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Audit your own schema against three questions: is the sort order aligned with the most common query predicate, are the types as narrow as they can be, and is anything stored that could be derived. Then make the single highest-value change and measure the query time before and after.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Handle the two-timestamp design properly: your tables carry an observation time and an availability time, and the as-of query filters on both. Check whether the physical layout supports that filter efficiently or whether every as-of query scans the whole table. Fix it if not.
:::
:::
